assumptions.label: SLATE's assumption, not DIA's published policy
assumptions.value: New Zealand charges GST on an online application from New Haven
assumptions.basis: The price DIA publishes is NZ$247 with GST (NZ-1). DIA's current costs page (blocked; search extracts) spares a non-resident for New Zealand tax applying online, and IRD makes that turn on a permanent place of abode in New Zealand (NZ-4), which SLATE doesn't keep for its student; DIA's 2022 papers said online applications from outside New Zealand don't attract GST (NZ-2), a wording its current page narrows. SLATE charged it from 2026-10-16. Off, every New Zealander applying from New Haven pays NZ$214.78.
assumptions.unavailableOrBlocked: unavailable for SLATE's student (the applicant's own facts); the page stating the current condition blocked
assumptions.shown: Papers' passport fine print, Not Confirmed; the guide's Another Country's Passport line; the tutorial

assumptions.label: SLATE's assumption
assumptions.value: New Zealand's urgent fee for an online application from overseas is the standard fee, NZ$214.78 before GST (NZ$247 with it)
assumptions.basis: DIA's 2022 schedule set the priority fee for New Zealand or online equal to the standard fee (NZ-2); Cabinet's 2025 increase applied to every passport fee alike (NZ-3); the 2025 regulations themselves (SL 2025/75) were behind an AWS WAF challenge, their figure seen only in a search extract (NZ$214.78). GST on it follows A1.
assumptions.shown: Papers' passport fine print, Not Confirmed; the guide; the urgent price drawn on Faster

assumptions.label: SLATE's assumption, not the state's published policy
assumptions.value: a Connecticut ID card issued to somebody not a citizen runs to the end of their lawful presence (the program's end at school, OPT's end on OPT), never past the seven years to a birthday
assumptions.basis: No statute, regulation or DMV page gives a term for the card the DMV doesn't verify (CT-1, CT-3, CT-4), and the 2005 bill that would have set this one failed (CT-2), so it isn't the law; the DMV's own limited-term REAL ID 'must align with the expiration date on the individual's legal status document(s)' (read 2026-10-16, brief 11); § 14-137-64a(c) lets the commissioner revoke the card once its holder is no longer entitled to be present; SLATE has run it so from 2026-10-10. Off, the card takes the published seven years to a birthday, still after SAVE and the mail, still non-verified.
assumptions.shown: Your ID on Papers; the guide's Connecticut's ID Card line; the tutorial

whenARuleChanges: A value is read when an application is made and what it sets is stored then: a card's expiry on the card, a fee in the ledger. Changed later, a card already issued or on its way keeps its date, a fee charged stands, a passport on its way comes as applied for, and the new value applies to what's applied for after; nothing recomputes on arrival, replacement or load. Correcting documents already held would take a dated migration in ONCE_ON_OPENING (src/engine/index.ts), which this pass doesn't make because no value was found wrong. Each is held by a test that turns the value (TEST SETUP) mid-play.
